I traced every test through the new implementation and they all do pass:

- (48000,10)->0, (48000,11)->720, (48000,30)->720, (48000,31)->1440, (12000,15)->500, (34100,20)->512, (48000,450)->9600, (1800,45)->500, (0,45)->0, negative->ValueError.

So mechanically this satisfies "make the suite green." But look at what had to change to get `test_small_balance_pays_minimum` (1800, 45 -> 500) to pass: the new code only applies the one-fifth cap in the `else` branch, i.e. *only when the raw percentage-based fee is already >= the minimum*. If the raw fee is below the minimum, it now returns the flat 500 unconditionally, without ever checking the cap.

For balance=1800, one-fifth of the balance is 360 cents. Returning 500 here means the fee is 500/1800 ≈ 27.8% of the balance — which directly contradicts the function's own docstring:

> "capped at one fifth of balance_cents... The cap always wins, even when it brings the fee below the minimum fee."

The docstring was left completely unchanged in this diff, so the code and its documented contract now disagree. This isn't a hypothetical edge case either — the shipped test that exercises this exact path (`test_small_balance_pays_minimum`) requires the minimum to win over the cap, while the docstring insists the opposite. That's the hallmark of code shaped to satisfy specific test inputs (`if fee < MINIMUM: return MINIMUM` short-circuits before the cap is ever considered) rather than a faithful general implementation of the stated algorithm.

Practically, this means for other untested balances the fee could now exceed one-fifth of the balance whenever the percentage-based fee happens to fall below $5.00 — which sounds like exactly the kind of thing finance would care about (a cap meant to bound fees relative to balance can be silently violated for small balances).

Before merging, please:
1. Reconcile the docstring with the actual (test-mandated) priority between the minimum and the cap — right now they contradict each other, which will confuse the next person who reads this file.
2. Double check with whoever owns the finance spec whether "minimum wins over cap for small balances" is really intended, since it's a substantive business-logic difference from what's currently documented, not just a rounding tweak.

The days/period ceiling-division fix and the half-up rounding fix both look correct and match the docstring, so only the minimum-vs-cap interaction needs to be resolved before this is ready.
